label: Run 1 · all 8 chats
note: Every chat of run 1 (one line of persona, the game's material as inspiration): the same pair, the same brief and the same prompt, each written by a different writer.

chat.variety.why: All eight chats run the same night in the same order. Reuben opens with a hat-tip and a fake alibi for replying in seconds (barometer, Lisbon kettle, espresso valve). Brick answers "hm.", times his reply and sends a numbered inventory that discloses the dorsal bump. Then come the spontaneity-versus-schedule fight, a pasted planning note followed by "Ignore that.", the Marguerite calendar, the Delphine 'normal voice' story, the cropped family portrait and turning sideways past the fridge. Each ends with a timestamped sex agenda, the question "what happens at [time]" answered by "nothing", a hand flat on the back, and boring talk about lentils or a radiator. Nearly every set piece recurs in more than two chats, far past the line's limit: the snapped heel with frozen peas, the tattoo gap left by a man forty minutes early, "we can just watch something", finishing in ninety seconds with one boot on, the ring light that kills the shadow, and present-tense narration so neither disappears. It scores 2 rather than 1 because a few chats move who holds the clipboard: in Coel, Brick bails using the vet voice; in Parker and Armstrong & Bain, Brick writes the agenda; in Saunders, Brick narrates in bed out of habit. These are re-assignments within one template, not different nights.
evidence: You put one flat hand on my back so I know I'm still on the mattress
you keep one hand flat on my back so I know I'm in the bed
she patted my hip and said "We can just watch something" in the kindest voice
chat.variety.raise: Have at least half the chats break the shared spine: no pasted note, no timed-agenda ending, or a different first discovery and turning point, so that no three-beat sequence and no stock line recurs in more than half of them.
